newsitem.title: UK: Texaco says expects N.Sea Captain start soon.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says expects N.Sea Captain start soon.

text.p: Texaco Inc said on Tuesday first oil from its Captain oilfield in British North Sea waters had been postponed for a third time.
"We're still waiting but we hope it's going to be any day now," said a spokeswoman.

Production at the 350-million barrel field was originally expected to begin late last year but an accident at the Spanish shipyard where the floating production and storage vessel (FPSO) was being built forced postponement to late January.
Problems commissioning the FPSO led to the date being put back to February, but final checks were still being completed, the spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Captain will pump heavy 20 degree API crude and is expected to reach peak production of some 60,000 barrels per day later this year.
Shuttle tankers will carry the crude direct to local refiners or for reloading at Scotland's Nigg Bay.
